record.question: Which of the following was the main reason for the decline of the Zawlbuk as an institution?
options: The British administration found it to be an obstacle to their colonial governance.
Village Chiefs could no longer financially support the institution.
People felt it had reduced relevance in modern life.
Christian missionaries prohibited it and aimed to abolish it.
record.explanation: The decline of the Zawlbuk is usually linked to the spread of Christianity and reduced relevance under changing social conditions, which fits the third printed option. The option wording and the historical basis are not fully verified, so this answer is tentative.
